app.title: NDT Lens · X-ray inspection with human-reviewed auto-labelling
app.summary: A person imports a batch of radiographs, tagging each batch with a workpiece group and a train, val or test split. Duplicate images are skipped. They pick one image, draw rectangles on it with a chosen defect class, and fix the coordinates or classes in a table. They then either save it as a draft or confirm it as ground truth; a confirmed image with no boxes counts as a defect-free sample. From the confirmed images they start a detector training run in the background and watch its validation curve and log. They then use the trained model to auto-label the images still waiting for review, correct and confirm those proposals, and export a ZIP of the confirmed dataset. A separate page runs a single image through either a heuristic candidate finder or a trained model and downloads the annotated image, a JSON report and a CSV of the boxes.

task.text: Build a reviewed set of bounding-box labels on radiographs, train an object detector on the confirmed labels, and use it to propose labels on new images for a person to correct and confirm.

data.text: A collection of grayscale X-ray images. Each image belongs to a workpiece group and a split, and carries rectangular boxes from a fixed set of defect classes plus a review status, a revision number and the model that proposed its boxes.
data.item: a radiograph image with its labelled bounding boxes

stage.text: labelling and reviewing defect boxes on radiographs to build training data for a detector

mechanism.text: On the annotation page, a status filter and an image picker choose one image. A canvas editor draws class-coloured boxes on that image, and an editable table below mirrors the boxes; confirm and draft buttons save them with a revision check. Further pages start background training from confirmed images only, auto-label the pending images with the chosen model, and export a ZIP; counters at the top track images, confirmations and boxes waiting for review.

field.text: object detection on industrial radiographs for non-destructive testing

workflow.name: label regions in images, train a detector on confirmed labels, and review its proposals

steps.here: Multi-file upload of PNG, JPEG, TIFF or BMP images with a workpiece/film group number and a train, val or test split. Images with identical pixels are skipped, and the new images can optionally be auto-labelled with the selected model.

steps.step: filter to the items that matter
steps.here: A scope radio (all, pending review, confirmed) narrows the image picker, which marks each image confirmed (✓) or pending (○) and shows its group, split and the model that proposed its boxes.

steps.step: select a stretch and label it with a category
steps.here: Pick a defect class (porosity, crack or inclusion), then drag rectangles on a zoomable canvas. Undo removes the last box and clear removes them all. A table beside it lets the person change a box's class or coordinates, or delete it.

steps.step: decide keep or drop for each item, with a reason
steps.here: 'Save and confirm' makes the boxes ground truth. 'Save draft' keeps them out of training. Confirming an image with no boxes records it as a reviewed normal sample. A save is refused if the image's revision has changed since it was opened.

steps.step: track progress toward a target or a total
steps.here: Counters show total images, confirmed images, model labels waiting for review and confirmed boxes. A readiness table counts images, confirmed images and workpiece groups in each split.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: A detector training run is started in a background process on a snapshot of confirmed images only, with a chosen number of epochs, image size, batch size, device and starting weights. Each run's record shows its status, a validation mAP curve and the tail of its log.

The selected model auto-labels every pending image, and the person corrects and confirms those labels on the annotation page. A ZIP holds the original images, annotated previews, YOLO labels, a dataset.yaml and a review manifest, and by default contains confirmed images only.

distinctive: Model predictions never become ground truth until a person confirms them: training snapshots copy confirmed images only, and batch auto-labelling skips images that are already confirmed.
Each image belongs to a workpiece group that can sit in only one of train, val or test, and identical-pixel images are rejected on import, so near-copies cannot leak across splits.
An empty box list means two different things: an image not yet reviewed, or a confirmed defect-free sample.
Saves check a revision number, so an older page cannot silently overwrite newer labels.

A separate single-image page compares the original radiograph side by side with the detections, from either a morphology heuristic (grey-level difference threshold and minimum area) or a trained model with a confidence threshold.
